text:
sara.k: Hey @people-ops — quick help please. Two folks on my team (Jamie and Luis) are expecting overlapping parental leaves in mid-July through September. I need a checklist for (1) paperwork/deadlines we should start now, (2) options for coverage (short-term contractor vs internal rotation), and (3) any payroll/benefits gotchas if both leaves overlap. Want to start planning before Q3 planning meeting.

people-ops: Thanks for the heads-up, Sara. High-level checklist: submit the Parental Leave Request form, confirm FMLA/state leave eligibility, attach birth/adoption paperwork after the event, and coordinate pay-topup enrollment if eligible. Preferred notice is 30–60 days for planning but we can handle shorter notices in special cases. Payroll cutoff notes below. Link: https://hr.redwood.example/forms/parental-leave

payroll: Quick payroll bits — request form should be in before the start date if possible. For pay-topup programs: enrollment needs to be processed before the payroll cycle that covers the first paid week (cutoff is the 15th). If the event happens before paperwork is complete, you can still file retroactive adjustments but it delays pay. Attach birth/adoption docs within 30 days to avoid benefits interruptions. For questions email payroll@redwood.example.

people-ops: For coverage options: 1) Short-term contractor (45–90 days) — requires hiring ops + procurement; allow ~3 weeks for contracting + 1 week for onboarding. 2) Internal rotation — cross-training and a documented runbook; no procurement overhead but needs manager time. 3) Split coverage — combine a part-time contractor with pair-rotations for critical features. If you want us to kick off contracting, file a short hiring ops request and mark it "short-term temp" so it routes to procurement.

maya: I can prioritize getting runbooks together. Suggest we document the 2 daily ops tasks and a single-weekhand-off checklist in a repo. Recommend pairing sessions in the two weeks before leave.

jamie: happy to write the runbook — can break into: oncall steps, deploy checklist, and monitoring alerts. I can carve out 3 half-days next week to doc + record quick Looms.

luis: I can do overlap coverage for the first 2 weeks of the other's leave if that helps, then we switch to the contractor for deep maintenance.

people-ops: Sample minimal coverage rota (feel free to copy):
```
Week 1-2: knowledge transfer + shadowing (Jamie/Luis pair with Maya)
Week 3-6: contractor onboard + Jamie/Luis hand off critical oncall
Week 7-12: contractor handles routine ops, internal team keeps ownership of roadmap
```

people-ops: Hiring ops checklist to start now: 1) headcount approval note from manager, 2) short role scoping doc, 3) preferred hourly budget, 4) procurement contact. We can fast-track if you mark it urgent.

sara.k: Perfect — can you start the hiring ops request and loop me in? Also confirm whether company leave pay stacks with state leave (e.g., CA/NY).

people-ops: We'll start the hiring ops ticket. On pay stacking: it depends on state programs. In many states the company top-up coordinates with state disability/parental pay; payroll will model combined payments to avoid overpayment. We'll confirm exact numbers for CA/NY for your specific dates once you submit the request form.

payroll: To expedite, send estimated start/end dates for both leaves and a copy of the employees' most recent paystubs if available. We'll draft projected cashflow for you.

hr-bot: Checklist created and attached to this thread: Parental Leave Request form, Manager handoff template, Contractor hiring spec template. (link: https://hr.redwood.example/checklists/parental-overlap) :white_check_mark:

maya: I'll schedule three 1-hr pairing sessions next Tue/Wed/Thu and add them to the calendar — invite Jamie and Luis.

jamie: thanks — will start the runbook doc and ping when the Looms are up.

people-ops: Filing hiring ops ticket now and cc'ing procurement. Expect initial response in 1–2 business days. If you want us to proceed with contractor outreach, include the max hourly rate in the ticket.

sara.k: Awesome, thanks everyone. I'll post the tentative dates here once I have confirmation from both folks (planning to aim for July 10 start for Jamie and July 24 for Luis).
